እንኳን ወደ Moral and Citizenship Education (MCED 1011) የChapter 2 Part 2 (ከክፍል 2.3.3 እስከ 2.3.3.3) ልዩ የቱቶሪያል ኖት በሰላም መጣችሁ! የEthioFresh የCivics ትምህርት ዝግጅት ቡድን ይህንን ኖት ያዘጋጀላችሁ ከሞጁሉ ጽሁፍ ተነስተን በፈተና ላይ 100% ውጤታማ እንድትሆኑና በA+ እንድትወጡ በማሰብ ነው። በዚህ ክፍል የዩቲሊታሪያኒዝም (Utilitarianism) ፍልስፍናን፣ የቤንታምን እና የሚልን ሀሳቦች መስመር በመስመር በጥልቀት እንመረምራለን። መልካም ጥናት!

2.3.3. Utilitarianism: Producing the best consequences


Utilitarianism is a normative teleological (consequentialist) ethical theory holding that an action is morally right if and only if it produces the greatest amount of overall happiness, pleasure, or welfare for the greatest number of individuals affected by that action. Unlike Ethical Egoism—which is a limited teleological theory focused strictly on maximizing outcomes for oneself or a limited group—Utilitarianism requires an impartial, broad calculation aimed at maximizing total societal goodness. The foundational axiom of this doctrine is best summarized by the famous maxim: "That action is best, which procures the greatest happiness for the greatest numbers."

Limitations of Traditional Moral Rules of Thumb:
The module explores why informal, intuitive moral guides are insufficient for resolving complex ethical dilemmas:

  • 1. 'Let your conscience be your guide': Conscience is subjective, variable, and often contradictory between individuals. If two individuals have conflicting conscience directives, relying on conscience leaves no objective standard to resolve the dispute.
  • 2. 'Do whatever is most loving': While love is a positive emotional disposition, it is emotionally biased and lacks structured fairness. Love alone cannot dictate how to distribute resources objectively when faced with competing claims (e.g., loving enemies vs. victims, or Auschwitz survivors loving Hitler).
  • 3. 'The Golden Rule (Do to others as you would have them do to you)': Helpful in everyday reciprocal interactions, but it cannot be taken literally without qualification and fails to specify priorities in complex resource distribution scenarios.

Module Case Study / Activity:
The Dying Millionaire in Jigjiga: A dying millionaire in Jigjiga asks you to deliver $2 million of his wealth to the Ethiopian Coffee Club in Addis Ababa to buy players. You promise to do so, but upon arrival in Addis Ababa, you see an advertisement from the Ethiopian Red Cross Society (ERCS) requesting $2 million to save 100,000 people from starvation and build a sustainable agricultural economy.

  • A Deontologist would insist on keeping the promise regardless of the outcome, viewing promise-breaking as intrinsically wrong.
  • A Consequentialist / Utilitarian calculation dictates breaking the promise because saving 100,000 lives creates exponentially greater well-being and reduces massive human suffering compared to aiding a sports club!

👉 ዩቲሊታሪያኒዝም (Utilitarianism) በውጤት ላይ የተመሰረተ (Consequentialist / Teleological) የስነ-ምግባር ቲዮሪ ሲሆን፣ የአንድን ድርጊት ትክክለኛነት የምንመዝነው በድርጊቱ በሚመጣው አጠቃላይ የደስታና የጥቅም መጠን ነው። ዋና መርሁም "የላቀ ደስታን ለብዙሃኑ ማረጋገጥ" (Greatest happiness for the greatest number) የሚለው ነው። ከኢጎይዝም የሚለየው ኢጎይዝም ለራስ ወይም ለተወሰነ ቡድን ጥቅም ብቻ ሲያስብ፣ ይህ ቲዮሪ ግን የሁሉንም ሰው ደስታ በእኩልነት ይመዝስናል። እንደ ሕሊና (Conscience)፣ ፍቅር (Love) እና ወርቃማው ሕግ (Golden Rule) ያሉ ባህላዊ መመሪያዎች ውስብስብ የማህበረሰብ ግጭቶች ሲፈጠሩ ግልጽና ወጥ የሆነ መፍትሄ መስጠት አይችሉም። ለምሳሌ በጅጅጋው ባለሃብት ጉዳይ ህሊናህ ቃልህን ጠብቅ ሊልህ ይችላል፣ ነገር ግን ዩቲሊታሪያኒዝም 100,000 የረሃብ ሰዎችን ማዳን የተሻለ ውጤት እንደሚያመጣ ያሳያል።

2.3.3.1. Classic Utilitarianism

Origins & Key Philosophical Thinkers:
The historical foundations of utilitarian reasoning trace back to the ancient Greek philosopher Epicurus (342–270 BCE), who posited that pleasure is the ultimate good ordained by nature and the standard by which we judge everything good. While Epicurus focused on individual personal experience of pleasure and pain (advocating a version of ethical egoism), his views inspired 18th-century thinkers who emphasized the notion of general happiness—pleasing consequences of actions that impact others and not just the individual.

The formal classical expressions of utilitarianism appear in the writings of two English philosophers and social reformers: Jeremy Bentham (1748–1832) and John Stuart Mill (1806–1873). They were the nonreligious ancestors of twentieth-century secular humanists, optimistic about human nature and our ability to solve problems without recourse to God. Engaged in legal and moral reform, they were impatient with the rule-bound character of law and morality in 18th- and 19th-century Great Britain and tried to make the law serve human needs and interests.

👉 ክላሲካል ዩቲሊታሪያኒዝም (Classic Utilitarianism) በ 18ኛው እና 19ኛው ክፍለ ዘመን በሁለቱ እንግሊዛውያን ፈላስፎች ጀረሚ ቤንታም (Jeremy Bentham) እና ጆን ስቱዋርት ሚል (John Stuart Mill) የተገነባ ነው። የሃሳቡ መነሻ የጥንቱ ግሪክ ፈላስፋ ኤፒኩረስ (Epicurus) ቢሆንም፣ ኤፒኩረስ ግን ትኩረቱ የግል ደስታ (Egoism) ላይ ነበር። ቤንታም እና ሚል ግን የሃይማኖት አሰራርን ሳይከተሉ (Secular humanists) ስነ-ምግባር እና ህግ የሰውን ልጅ ችግር ለመፍታትና አጠቃላይ የህብረተሰብ ደስታን ለመጨመር መዋል አለባቸው ብለው ተከራክረዋል።

2.3.3.2. Jeremy Bentham: Quantity over Quality

The Two Core Principles & Hedonic Calculus:
Bentham articulated two main features of utilitarianism:

  • 1. The consequentialist principle (or its teleological aspect): States that the rightness or wrongness of an act is determined by the goodness or badness of the results that flow from it. It is the end, not the means that counts; the end justifies the means.
  • 2. The utility principle (or its hedonic aspect): States that the only thing that is good in itself is some specific type of state (for example, pleasure, happiness, welfare).

Hedonistic utilitarianism views pleasure as the sole good and pain as the sole evil. An act is right if it either brings about more pleasure than pain or prevents pain, and wrong if it brings about more pain than pleasure or prevents pleasure from occurring. Bentham invented a scheme for measuring pleasure and pain called the Hedonic Calculus. The quantitative score for any pleasure or pain experience is obtained by summing the seven aspects of a pleasurable or painful experience:

  • 1. Intensity: How strong is the pleasure or pain?
  • 2. Duration: How long does the experience last?
  • 3. Certainty: How likely is it that the pleasure or pain will occur?
  • 4. Nearness (Propinquity): How soon will the outcome happen?
  • 5. Fruitfulness (Fecundity): Will the act lead to further pleasures of the same kind?
  • 6. Purity: Is the pleasure free from accompanying pain?
  • 7. Extent: How many individuals are impacted by the decision?

Quantitative Application & Calculation:
Adding up the amounts of pleasure and pain for each possible act and then comparing the scores enables us to decide which act to perform. In the dying millionaire example (giving money to Ethiopian Coffee Club vs. famine victims), giving to famine victims causes at least 3 million hedons (units of happiness), whereas giving to the club causes less than 1,000 hedons, creating a clear moral obligation to give to famine relief. Bentham's system is simple, commonsensical, and scientific: it makes quantitative measurements and applies the principle impartially, giving no special treatment based on race, gender, personal relationship, or religion.

👉 ጀረሚ ቤንታም ደስታን በመጠን (Quantity) ብቻ ይለካል። ደስታን በቁጥር ለማስላት Hedonic Calculus የተባለውን 7 ነጥቦች ያሉት ቀመር አዘጋጀ። እነሱም፦ ጥንካሬው (Intensity)፣ ቆይታው (Duration)፣ እርግጠኝነቱ (Certainty)፣ ቅርብነቱ (Nearness)፣ ተጨማሪ ደስታ የማስገኘት አቅሙ (Fruitfulness)፣ ከህመም የጸዳ መሆኑ (Purity) እና የሚዳረሰው ሰው ብዛት (Extent) ናቸው። ቤንታም ደስታን በHedons (የደስታ መለኪያ) በማስላት ለብዙሃኑ የሚተርፈውን መምረጥ እንዳለብን ያስተምራል።
💡 Exam Hint: በፈተና ላይ "Hedonic Calculus" ወይም "Quantity over Quality" ከሚለው ሀሳብ ጋር ተያይዞ የሚመጣው ስም Jeremy Bentham ነው። የ 7ቱን መለኪያዎች ስሞች በደንብ ያዙ!

2.3.3.3. John Stuart Mill: Quality over Quantity

Eudaimonistic Utilitarianism & Qualitative Distinction:
To meet objections and save utilitarianism from the charge of being a "pig philosophy", Bentham's successor, John Stuart Mill, sought to distinguish happiness from mere sensual pleasure. His version of the theory is often called eudaimonistic utilitarianism (from the Greek eudaimonia, meaning "happiness"). He defines happiness in terms of certain types of higher-order pleasures or satisfactions such as intellectual, aesthetic, and social enjoyments, as well as in terms of minimal suffering. There are two types of pleasures:

  • The lower, or elementary pleasures: include eating, drinking, sexuality, resting, and sensuous titillation. Although more intensely gratifying, they also lead to pain when overindulged in.
  • The higher pleasures: tend to be more long term, continuous, and gradual, including high culture, scientific knowledge, intellectuality, and creativity.

Mill's Famous Axiom & Human Nature:
Mill argued that the higher, or more refined, pleasures are superior to the lower ones: "It is better to be a human being dissatisfied than a pig satisfied; better to be Socrates dissatisfied than a fool satisfied." Humans are the kind of creatures who require more to be truly happy; they want the lower pleasures, but they also want deep friendship, intellectual ability, culture, the ability to create and appreciate art, knowledge, and wisdom.

The point is not merely that humans wouldn't be satisfied with what satisfies a pig, but that somehow the quality of the higher pleasures is better. Happiness is not a life of rapture, but moments of such, in an existence made up of few and transitory pains, many and various pleasures, with a decided predominance of the active over the passive. Mill is clearly pushing the boundaries of the concept of "pleasure" by emphasizing higher qualities such as knowledge, intelligence, freedom, friendship, love, and health. In fact, one might even say that his litmus test for happiness really has little to do with actual pleasure and more to do with a non-hedonic cultivated state of mind.

👉 ጆን ስቱዋርት ሚል የቤንታምን ሀሳብ በማሻሻል ደስታ በጥራት (Quality) ይለያል አለ (Eudaimonistic Utilitarianism)። ሚል ደስታን በሁለት ይከፍላል፦ ዝቅተኛ ደስታዎች (መብላት፣ መጠጣት፣ አካላዊ እረፍት) እና ከፍተኛ ደስታዎች (እውቀት፣ ስነ-ጥበብ፣ የላቀ አእምሯዊና ማህበራዊ ግንኙነት)። ሚል ሲናገር "የረካ አሳማ ከመሆን ያልረካ ሰው መሆን ይበልጣል፤ የረካ ሞኝ ከመሆን ያልረካ ሶቅራጥስ መሆን ይበልጣል" ብሏል። የሰው ልጅ እውነተኛ ደስታ ከፍ ካሉ አእምሯዊና ስነ-ምግባራዊ እሴቶች ጋር የተያያዘ ስለሆነ ደስታ ጊዜያዊ ስሜት ብቻ ሳይሆን ያደገ አእምሯዊና መንፈሳዊ ሁኔታ (Cultivated state of mind) ነው ብሎ ያምናል።
